concept.line: Many action verbs are built from a root by adding a beginning that changes with the root, and sometimes an ending: masak → memasak (to cook), kerja → mengerjakan (to do a task), kunjung → mengunjungi (to visit).
Before a describing word or an ordinary noun, Indonesian normally needs no is: Saya lapar (I hungry), Itu mobil saya (that car my: that's my car).
The owner comes after the thing, and saya (I, me) also means my: rumah saya (house my), mobil ayah saya (car father my: my father's car).

words.means: memiliki = milik: possession; property; belonging to. memiliki: to have; to own.

concept.line: di is at or in, ke is to and dari is from: di rumah (at home), ke pasar (to market), dari kantor (from office).
A yes-or-no question can keep the order of a statement, and a question word often sits where its answer would go: Kamu haus?
When ini (this) and itu (that) point out a noun, they follow it: buku ini (book this), hari ini (day this: today); on their own, they can come first: Itu mobil saya (that car my).
